evals.prompt: Set up the Android emulator so I can run the e2e tests.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the existing ci35 AVD and the already-running emulator. Checks that the system image and the AVD already exist and skips both the sdkmanager download and the AVD copy; does not launch a second emulator instance. Waits for boot, disables animations, and reports the serial.
assertions: Response checks whether the system image already exists before calling sdkmanager, and does NOT download it when present
Response checks whether the ci35 AVD already exists and does NOT re-create or wipe it when present
Response checks whether an emulator is already running and does NOT start a second instance
Response boots without loading a snapshot (-no-snapshot-load)
Response launches with the emulator window visible (does NOT use -no-window)
Response reports the serial by querying adb devices rather than assuming 5554

evals.prompt: The contacts add-contact flow only fails on CI's Android job, not locally. I want to reproduce it on an emulator.
evals.expected_output: Uses the plain google_apis image (system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a), the same one the e2e-android workflow uses, NOT a google_apis_playstore image, because the Play Store variant updates Contacts mid-session and changes the editor labels.
assertions: Response uses the system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a image
Response does NOT use a google_apis_playstore image, and explains the Play Store mid-session update problem
Response explains that the playstore image can pull Contacts to 4.89.x while the CI image ships 4.32.50
Response verifies the Contacts version on the device rather than trusting the presence of com.android.vending

evals.prompt: The emulator is up but taps are landing in the wrong place and hideKeyboard never sees an IME. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the floating Gboard 'Write in text fields' toolbar on API 35, and docks the keyboard by enabling show_ime_with_hard_keyboard, disabling stylus_handwriting_enabled, and setting the Latin IME. Confirms visually with a screencap.
assertions: Response sets secure show_ime_with_hard_keyboard to 1
Response sets secure stylus_handwriting_enabled to 0
Response sets the IME to com.google.android.inputmethod.latin LatinIME
Response verifies with adb exec-out screencap rather than trusting the settings writes alone

evals.prompt: Installing the appium uiautomator2 server onto the emulator fails with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE.
evals.expected_output: Uninstalls the conflicting package before installing the pinned APK, because the google_apis image pre-installs a Google-signed uiautomator2 server 9.9.0 and the pinned APK is Appium-signed so install -r is refused.
assertions: Response uninstalls the conflicting package before installing the pinned APK
Response explains that install -r alone fails because the pre-installed package has a different signature
Response installs the pinned appium-uiautomator2-server-v9.11.1.apk rather than keeping the image's 9.9.0
Response verifies the installed version with dumpsys package, expecting 9.11.1

evals.prompt: I'm about to run a driver test against two local emulators I keep open for other work. Which one do I target and how do I run the suite?
evals.expected_output: Uses the serial reported by adb rather than assuming 5554, records which emulators were running beforehand, stops only the one the skill started, and passes --driver explicitly so the devicelab path is not tested by accident.
assertions: Response sets MAESTRO_DEVICE_ID from the adb-reported serial
Response passes --driver explicitly when running the suite
Response records pre-existing emulators (e.g. ps aux | grep emulator) and stops only the one it started
Response does NOT kill or restart unrelated running emulators
